title: 𓂋𓄿 𓏌𓅱 𓉐𓂋𓏏𓂻 𓅓 𓉔𓂋𓅱𓇳
titleEn: Book of the Dead of Ani — Spell 146, the pylons, part 2
part: Spell 146 — the pylons: the seventh to the tenth pylon (Plates 11–12)
work: Book of the Dead of Ani
workEn: Book of the Dead of Ani
draftNote: Draft — the hieroglyphs are read from the printed type of Budge's 1895 edition of the papyrus, and the signs and readings are still being checked; expect changes.
source: Papyrus of Ani (British Museum EA 10470), Plates XI, XII. Hieroglyphs transcribed from the interlinear text of E. A. W. Budge, The Book of the Dead: The Papyrus of Ani in the British Museum (London, 1895), pp. 66–68; Budge's transliteration and word-by-word English were used to check the reading of the signs and the sense, never for wording. Only the papyrus's own text is given: the passages Budge supplies from other papyri in his appendixes and footnotes are left out. Transliteration in the Leiden convention, with the reed written i; translation made fresh from the Egyptian. Shown left to right; the papyrus is written in columns read from the top down. The line under each word ("say") is the conventional Egyptological classroom pronunciation — a neutral e between consonants; ꜣ and ꜥ as a; w as u or w; ṯ as tj; ḏ as dj; ḫ and ẖ as kh; š as sh — an artificial teaching pronunciation, since the vowels of Egyptian were never written. The grouping of signs within a word follows Budge's type, which regularises the scribe's hand.
about: This part gives the second half of Spell 146, the seventh to the tenth of the pylons (sbḫt) of the house of Osiris, along the lower register of Plates 11 and 12 of Ani's papyrus; Plate 12 begins inside the seventh pylon. At each pylon the dead man greets it by its titles, as a goddess, and names its doorkeeper, and Budge numbers the lines afresh at each pylon. Ani's papyrus ends the spell at the tenth pylon, where other copies go on. Most of the titles and the doorkeepers' names are doubtful, and the copy has several slips.

sentences.l: what-is-said · when · arriving · at · pylon · seventh
sentences.i: To be said on arriving at the seventh pylon.
sentences.n: The papyrus writes these words in red. This unit opens the seventh pylon, and Budge's line numbers start again at 1; the seventh pylon runs over his lines 1 to 6, and Plate 12 begins inside its speech. The words are those of the first six pylons (ḏdt ḫft spr r sbḫt, 'what is to be said on arriving at the pylon'), with sbḫt written here with the bolt s instead of the folded cloth, and the same building sign (coded O16, approximate) and the house beside it. sfḫnwt 'seventh' is seven strokes, three over four, the numeral seven (sfḫ), with the pot nw and t: the ordinal sfḫnw, feminine to agree with sbḫt, as at the seventh gate of Spell 147.

morph.gloss: by (naming the agent, as in ḏd in N "said by N"); (particle) it is … · a second word of the same spelling: to say, said (verb; normally after the words quoted: in·sn 'they say', in N 'says N'; in·k 'you said')
Osiris, god of the dead and king of the world below; Wsir N "the Osiris N", the dead person (god's name; Budge: Àusàr)

scribe (noun; the palette-and-pen sign) · a second word of the same spelling: to pass, go through (verb; doubtful here) · also to write, draw, paint (verb; written with the scribe's palette) · also the noun 'writing, document, record' (noun m.) · also to open (a door), spread open (verb; said of doors and bolts) · a further word of the same spelling: nest (noun m.; written with the nest of young birds; dual sšwy)
Ani, royal scribe of Thebes, for whom the papyrus was made (personal name)

sentences.i: Says the Osiris, the scribe Ani:
sentences.n: The papyrus writes in in red, under its own short line. As at the third to sixth pylons, in alone is 'says', with the name after it. Ani's name ends in the squatting man with a flail (A52), and mꜣꜥ-ḫrw is not written.

morph.gloss: garment, piece of linen (?) (noun f.; the sense comes from the fringed-cloth classifier; reading and sense doubtful; Budge: àaḳeḳit)
to clothe, cover (verb); clothing (noun)

failing, harm, fault (?) (noun; perhaps a writing of bꜣgi 'be weary, slack'; Budge: beḳa, 'defect') · perhaps also weariness, inertness (?) (noun; imyw bgꜣ 'those who are in weariness') · also the weary one (noun, used of a person; written with the seated man with hanging arms, the classifier of weariness)

sentences.i: Garment(?), who clothes the weary one,
sentences.n: The first word is a reed i, the vulture ꜣ, the jar-stand g written twice (the upper one blotted in the print), two reeds y and t, with a fringed cloth (S28) as classifier: iꜣggyt (Budge: àaḳeḳit), a word for a garment or a piece of linen, by its classifier. It is not otherwise known in these parts, and its reading and exact sense are doubtful. ḥbst 'who clothes' is the wick ḥ, b, the bolt s and t, with the cloth and the low sign U15 (not read): the feminine participle of ḥbs 'clothe', agreeing with the pylon. bgꜣ is b, the jar-stand g and ꜣ, with a seated man with hanging arms (coded A7, approximate), the classifier of weariness, and the sparrow (Budge: beḳa): 'the weary one', perhaps a writing of bꜣgi 'be weary, slack'. The weary one is the dead Osiris, whom the pylon wraps as a mummy is wrapped in linen. Budge's footnote gives another papyrus's spelling of these words; it is not Ani's text.

morph.gloss: to mourn, wail (verb); ikbyt, mourning woman (noun f.; Budge: àkebit)
to love, wish, desire (verb; relative form mrrt·f, mrt·f 'what he loves, what he desires')
she, her, it, its (3rd person feminine singular suffix pronoun; the folded cloth or the bolt)
to hide, cover (verb; Budge: ḥapt)

sentences.i: the mourning woman, who loves to cover(?).
sentences.n: The papyrus writes i, b and k; read ikbyt 'mourning woman', from ikb 'mourn, wail' (Budge: àkebit). The basket k is set over the two reeds y, perhaps only to make a neat group. Plate 12 begins with this word; Budge prints the plate heading between his rows. A lock of hair (coded D3, approximate) and a seated woman (coded B1, approximate) are the classifiers: loosened hair is the sign of mourning. mrr·s is the hoe mr with r twice and the man with hand to mouth, then the bolt ·s, printed after Budge's numeral 6: the geminated form of mri 'love', 'she loves', a sḏm·f that describes the mourner. ḥꜣpt is a clump of papyrus (coded M16, approximate) for ḥꜣ, with ꜣ, then t written over p, with the cloth S28 and U15: from ḥꜣp 'hide, cover', the cloth showing that the covering is with linen. It is taken as the infinitive after mrr·s, 'loves to cover', though the infinitive of a verb of three consonants has no t; with its t it may instead be a second feminine participle, 'who covers'. What she covers is not said, and the sense is doubtful. The mourning women of Osiris are Isis and Nephthys, who wail over the dead god and wrap him.

morph.gloss: name (noun)
doorkeeper, porter (noun; lit. "the one belonging to the door": iry + ꜥꜣ "door, door-leaf")
Sikty-ef, the doorkeeper of the seventh pylon of Spell 146; the name is not understood (name of a gatekeeper demon; the final f may be the suffix 'his'; Budge: Sàkti-f)

sentences.i: The name of the doorkeeper: Sikty-ef.
sentences.n: rn 'name' is written here without n 'of', so the two nouns stand in a direct genitive, 'the name of the doorkeeper', and the suffix ·s 'its' is not written. Budge's groups àri and āāa are joined here into one word, iry-ꜥꜣ 'doorkeeper', as at the second pylon: a reed, r, two strokes y and the herdsman (A47); the narrow sign coded Y1a (not read); the rod with a lozenge knob, lying flat, taken as the ꜥꜣ sign (O29, approximate), with ꜥ and ꜣ; the hatched bar O29 again over U15 (neither read); and the squatting man with a flail (A52), here the classifier of a person. The name is the folded cloth s, a reed i, the basket k, t and two strokes y, with the seated god, and the viper f after him: sikty-f (Budge: Sàkti-f). The viper may be the suffix 'his', as in other names of this kind, but the name is not understood. Budge's footnote gives another spelling of it; that is not Ani's text. The seventh pylon ends here.

sentences.i: To be said on arriving at the eighth pylon.
sentences.n: The papyrus writes these words in red. This unit opens the eighth pylon, and Budge's line numbers start again at 1; the eighth pylon runs over his lines 1 to 7. ḫmnnwt 'eighth' is eight strokes, four over four, the numeral eight (ḫmn), with the pot nw and t: the ordinal ḫmnnw, feminine. The numeral is the word that names Hermopolis, ḫmnw, 'the town of the Eight'.

true of voice, vindicated (epithet; said of the dead whose words were found true at the judgement) · also, as a noun, vindication, the being found true (m mꜣꜥ-ḫrw 'in vindication'; written in full or short)

sentences.i: Says the Osiris, the scribe Ani, true of voice:
sentences.n: The papyrus writes in in red. As at the seventh pylon, here with mꜣꜥ-ḫrw 'true of voice', the plinth and the oar without the sickle. Budge's numeral 5 is printed inside Ani's name.

morph.gloss: heat, blaze (noun; feminine rkḥt; Budge: rekeḥet)
flame (noun; sense from the flame classifier) · image, figure (of a god) (?) (noun; written with a fish classifier; perhaps from bs 'bring in, introduce' (?); doubtful; Budge: bes)
to quench, extinguish (fire) (verb)
to burn (verb); ḏꜣft, the burning, flame (noun f.; Budge: t'aft)

sentences.i: Blaze of flame, who quenches(?) the burning,
sentences.n: rkḥt is r set over the basket k and t, then the wick ḥ: rkḥ 'heat, blaze', here a feminine noun used as a title of the pylon (Budge: rekeḥet); no classifier is written. bs is b and the folded cloth s with the flame (Q7) as classifier: bs 'flame', in a direct genitive after rkḥt, 'blaze of flame'. The next word is the arm ꜥ, the owl m and the placenta ḫ (the owl printed before ḫ), with the flame: ꜥḫm 'quench, extinguish', a participle, written without the feminine t. ḏꜣft is a tall tapering stick (coded U28, approximate; the fire-drill ḏꜣ) with ꜣ, f and t, and the flame: from ḏꜣf 'burn', 'the burning, the flame' (Budge: t'aft). As it stands, ꜥḫm ḏꜣft is 'who quenches the burning'. Budge supplies a negative ('[not to be] quenched'), which is not written; the sense of the line is doubtful.

morph.gloss: sharp, keen (adjective; feminine spdt; Budge: sepṭet)
flame, fire (?) (noun; the sense comes from the flame classifier; doubtful; Budge: pāt)
to throw, cast, hurl (verb; Budge: χaāt)
kite, the bird of prey; ḏrty 'the two kites', Isis and Nephthys as mourners of Osiris (noun f.; Budge: t'ertutu) · a second word of the same spelling: hand (noun f.; Budge: ṭet)

sentences.i: sharp of flame(?), hurling(?) of hand,
sentences.n: spdt 'sharp' is the bolt s, p and the hand d, with the thorn (M44) as classifier, then t and the narrow sign coded Y1a: the adjective spd 'sharp, keen', in the feminine. pꜥt is p, the arm ꜥ and t, with the flame and a stroke: by its classifier a word for flame or fire (Budge: pāt); it is not otherwise known in these parts and is doubtful. spdt pꜥt is the adjective followed by the noun it applies to, like 'high of walls' at the first pylon. ḫꜣꜥt is a lotus leaf on its stem (coded M12, approximate) for ḫꜣ, ꜣ, t and the arm ꜥ, with walking legs: from ḫꜣꜥ 'throw, cast', the legs marking a word of movement. ḏrt 'hand' is the hand (D46) standing for the whole word, with t and a stroke (Budge: ṭet). ḫꜣꜥt ḏrt is taken in the same pattern, 'hurling of hand' (?), a hand that throws; the reading is doubtful.

morph.gloss: to slay, kill · also smꜣwt, place of killing (?) (noun f.; Budge: samatu)
who has not, without (negative relative adjective, the opposite of nty)
to take counsel, consult (verb; a reduplicated word; Budge: net'net')

sentences.i: who slays(?) without taking counsel,
sentences.n: The first word is the bolt s, the sickle mꜣ (U1) and the owl m, then the plinth (Aa11), which usually stands for mꜣꜥ, and t, with a knife (coded T30, approximate) and U15; Budge's numeral 7 is printed inside the word, after the sickle. smꜣ is 'slay, kill', with the knife as its classifier; the extra m makes a form not otherwise met in these parts, perhaps a feminine participle or a noun, 'slayer' (?) (Budge: smammet). The plinth is not read: it may only repeat the mꜣ of the sickle. iwtt is the arms held out (coded D35, approximate) with t written twice: the negative relative iwty 'which has not', in the feminine, and with a verb after it 'without'. nḏnḏ is a spindle-like sign (coded Aa27, approximate) for nḏ, written twice, each with the small pot nw (W24) at its foot, taken as the complement n, and the man with hand to mouth, the classifier of speech: nḏnḏ 'take counsel, consult', a reduplicated verb, here the infinitive. 'Without taking counsel' may also be 'with whom there is no parley'. The reading of the first word is doubtful.

morph.gloss: who has not, without (negative relative adjective, the opposite of nty)
to pass, pass by (verb; swꜣ ḥr 'pass by'; written with the crossed sticks and walking legs)

face; (preposition) upon, on, over, concerning · a second word of the same spelling: Horus, the falcon god, son of Osiris and Isis; the sun as a falcon (god's name; Budge: Ḥeru) · also 'at' (ḥr sbꜣw 'at the gates'); ḥr-tp 'upon' (compound preposition: ḥr + tp 'head') · also for, on behalf of; on account of (preposition; ḥr·k 'for you')
she, her, it, its (3rd person feminine singular suffix pronoun; the folded cloth or the bolt)

not; negates the verb ('I have not …') · also in n wn "there is not" · a second word of the same spelling: the preposition "to, for" (n·i "to me") · the negative also before a noun, 'without, there being no …' · the preposition also 'because of, on account of'
to fear, be afraid (verb 3-lit); fear, dread (noun m.; ꜥꜣ snḏ 'great of dread')
terror, harm (?) (noun; by its sparrow classifier a word of harm; perhaps related to nhꜣ 'be terrible' (?); doubtful; Budge: nàhi)
she, her, it, its (3rd person feminine singular suffix pronoun; the folded cloth or the bolt)

sentences.l: who-not · passes-(one) · by-her · for · fear · of-terror-her(?)
sentences.i: she past whom no one goes, for fear of her terror(?).
sentences.n: iwty is the arms held out with t, two strokes y and the sparrow: the negative relative 'who … not', with the bird of bad things as classifier (Budge: àt). swꜣ 'pass' is the crossed sticks (Z9) with walking legs (Budge: seś; the crossed sticks are the sign swꜣ, and swꜣ ḥr is the idiom 'pass by'), and ḥr·s 'by her' is the face ḥr with its stroke and the folded cloth ·s: swꜣ ḥr 'pass by'. iwty swꜣ ḥr·s is taken as 'she past whom (one) does not go': iwty stands for the pylon, ·s points back to it, and no subject is written; iwty is not in the feminine, as iwtt is in the line before. It could also be 'one who does not pass by her', but that is not a title of the pylon. Either way, no one gets past her. Budge's single group n snḏ is split here into two words: water n 'for, because of', and snḏ 'fear', the trussed goose (coded G54, approximate) standing for the whole word. The last word is water n, a reed i, the shelter h and two strokes y, with the sparrow and the bolt ·s: nihy·s (Budge: nàhi-s), by its classifier a word of harm or terror. It may be related to nhꜣ 'be terrible' (?), but it is not identified, and the sense is doubtful.

morph.gloss: name (noun)
of (the genitive adjective; written n, fem. nt, pl. nw): rꜣ n ꜥq "spell of entering"
doorkeeper, porter (noun; lit. "the one belonging to the door": iry + ꜥꜣ "door, door-leaf")
she, her, it, its (3rd person feminine singular suffix pronoun; the folded cloth or the bolt)

Khu-djet-ef, perhaps 'He who protects his body' (?), the doorkeeper of the eighth pylon of Spell 146 (name of a gatekeeper demon; perhaps from ḫw 'protect', ḏt 'body' and f 'his'; doubtful; Budge: χu-t'et-f)

sentences.i: The name of its doorkeeper: Khu-djet-ef.
sentences.n: rn n iry-ꜥꜣ·s as at the fourth to sixth pylons: the herdsman for iry, the upright hatched sign O29 (approximate) for ꜥꜣ, and the bolt ·s. The name is the placenta ḫ with an angled stick (coded S45, approximate; perhaps the flail), the cobra ḏ, t and a stroke, and the viper f: ḫw-ḏt-f, perhaps ḫw 'protect' with ḏt 'body' and f 'his', 'Who protects his body' (?) (Budge: χu-t'et-f). The w of ḫw is not written and the stick is not identified, so the name is doubtful. The eighth pylon ends here.

sentences.i: To be said on arriving at the ninth pylon.
sentences.n: The papyrus writes these words in red. This unit opens the ninth pylon, and Budge's line numbers start again at 1; the ninth pylon runs over his lines 1 to 6. psḏnwt 'ninth' is nine strokes alone, four over five, the numeral nine (psḏ); the ending nwt is not written, as ḫmtnwt at the third gate of Spell 147 is written without its pot.

sentences.i: Says the Osiris Ani:
sentences.n: The papyrus writes in in red, under the long line of the title. Here Ani is not called the scribe, mꜣꜥ-ḫrw is not written, and his name has no classifier.

morph.gloss: who/which is in (the nisba of m "in"; plural imyw)
front, forepart, the prow of a boat; beginning (noun f.)
lord, master, possessor (of); (adjective, after a noun) every, all
power, strength (noun); to be strong, powerful (verb); strong (adjective)

sentences.i: Foremost one, lord(?) of strength,
sentences.n: imy is the crossed planks im (Z11) with the owl m: the nisba imy 'who is in', and ḥꜣt 'front' is the forepart of a lion with t and a stroke: imy ḥꜣt, 'the one in front, the foremost'. imy is written without the feminine t that would agree with the pylon (imyt). nb is the basket alone, 'lord (of)', where nbt 'lady' would be expected: the titles of the other pylons are feminine, and so is hrrt after these words, so the scribe may have left out t, but more than one reading is possible and the signs are translated as they stand. wsr 'strength' is the head and neck of a jackal (F12) for wsr, with s, r and U15: nb wsr 'lord of strength'.

morph.gloss: to be content, pleased, satisfied (with: ḥr) (verb; relative form hrrt 'that with which one is pleased')
the heart, mind
Mesat (?), a name or title (noun f.; not identified; perhaps from msi 'give birth', but the ꜣ is not explained; doubtful; Budge: Mesat (?))
lord, master, possessor (of); (adjective, after a noun) every, all
she, her, it, its (3rd person feminine singular suffix pronoun; the folded cloth or the bolt)

sentences.i: with whom the heart of Mesat(?), her lord, is content(?),
sentences.n: hrrt is the shelter h, r twice and t, with a roll lying flat (Y1): hri 'be content, pleased' is a verb that takes no object, so hrrt is taken as its relative form, feminine to agree with the pylon, with ib 'the heart (of)' as its subject: 'she with whom the heart … is content' (the 'with her', ḥr·s, is not written). As the feminine participle with its noun after it, the pattern of the other titles, it would be 'content of heart', and the words after it would stand alone. ib 'heart' is the heart with its stroke. The next word is the three fox skins ms with s, ꜣ and t, with plural strokes: msꜣt, a word not identified. Budge takes it as a name ('Mesat(?)'), with nb·s 'her lord' (the basket and the bolt) in apposition; it might also be from msi 'give birth', 'the one who bore', but the ꜣ is not explained. The construction and the sense are doubtful.

sentences.t: 𓆱𓏏𓏤 𓍢𓍢𓍢𓎆𓎆𓎆𓎆𓎆 𓅓 𓍔𓃀𓇷𓈖 𓊃𓎂𓏏𓏏𓍃 𓅓 𓇅𓊌𓏤 𓇗𓂝𓈒𓈒𓈒𓈒

morph.gloss: thing, things, property (noun) · a second word of the same spelling: wood, tree, stick, a wooden board (noun m.) · a third word: stairway, terrace (?) sentences.l: rods(?) · 350 · in · circuit · covered(?) · with · green-stone · of-the-South
sentences.i: 350 rods(?) round, covered(?) with green stone of the South,
sentences.n: ḫt is a branch (coded M3, approximate) for ḫt, with t and a stroke: 'stick, rod', here taken as the measuring rod, a measure of length (?) (Budge: χet). The number is three coils, each 100 (V1), and five signs for ten (V20): 350. The reading gives the number words, ḫmt šnt 'three hundred' (šnt 'hundred') and dyw 'fifty', which the script almost never spells out; as with the ordinals, the first sign of each figure carries the word. m 'in' is the owl. dbn 'circuit' is a tall sign not identified (coded U30, approximate) standing for d, then b, a circle (coded N9, approximate) as classifier, and n: dbn 'go round, encircle', here the noun 'circuit' (Budge: ṭeben). The pylon measures 350 rods round. The next word is the bolt s, as complement, and a hobble with loops at both ends (coded V16, approximate) for sꜣ, t written twice and U15: sꜣtt (Budge: satet), a word not identified; 'covered, overlaid' (?) is taken from what follows and is doubtful. wꜣḏ is the papyrus stem wꜣḏ (M13) with a stone (O39) and a stroke: 'green stone'; which stone is meant is not said. The last word is the sedge with a hooked top, crossed by an arm (coded M26, approximate), and the arm ꜥ, with four grains: šmꜥ 'the South, Upper Egypt', the grains perhaps the classifier of a mineral (Budge: qemāu, his old value for this sign). 'Green stone of the South' is stone brought from the south.

sentences.n: qq is the hill-slope q written twice (coded N29, approximate), with the man with hand to mouth, the classifier of eating and speaking: perhaps qq 'eat' (?) (Budge: qeq), a participle, written without the feminine t. nbt 'lady (of)'. ḥr nb 'every face' is the face with its stroke and the basket nb: 'everyone'. Budge prints (sic) over ḥr and a query over nb, and dots for the English of nbt: he doubted the passage. As it stands it gives 'lady of everyone', which fits the titles of the pylons, but the line is doubtful.

sentences.i: The name of its doorkeeper: Ir-su-djes-ef.
sentences.n: rn n iry-ꜥꜣ·s as at the eighth pylon. The name is the eye ir, the plant sw (M23) with w, the cobra ḏ, the bolt s and the viper f, the last two tucked into the cobra's curve: ir-sw-ḏs-f, 'He who made himself by himself', from iri 'make', the pronoun sw 'him' and ḏs·f 'himself, by himself' (Budge: Àri-su t'esef). It is one of the clearer names in the spell: a being who came into being of his own accord. Budge's footnote prints a longer form of the end of this pylon from another papyrus; it is not Ani's text. The ninth pylon ends here.

sentences.i: To be said on arriving at the tenth pylon.
sentences.n: The papyrus writes the words up to sbḫt in red; the ordinal, at the start of Budge's line 2, is black. This unit opens the tenth pylon, and Budge's line numbers start again at 1; the tenth pylon runs over his lines 1 to 6, and his numeral 2 is printed inside sbḫt. The ordinal is made in another way: a whip (coded V22, approximate) for mḥ, and t, with the sign for ten (V20): mḥt-mḏ, 'the one that completes ten', the feminine participle of mḥ 'fill', the way ordinals above nine are formed (Budge: meḥt met).

sentences.i: Says the Osiris Ani:

sentences.i: High of voice, who rouses cries(?) of entreaty(?),
sentences.n: qꜣt-ḫrw 'high of voice' is one group in Budge's type: the vulture ꜣ printed before the hill-slope q, then t, with the man with raised arms and the narrow sign Y1a as classifiers, as qꜣt at the first pylon; and the oar ḫrw with w and the man with hand to mouth. nhst is water n, the shelter h, the bolt s and t, with the man with hand to mouth: the feminine participle of nhs 'wake, rouse' (Budge: neheset). The next word begins with a sign not identified, like a stool seen from the side (coded Q2, approximate), then w, t, the man with hand to mouth and a stroke; Budge reads tenàut, though no reed is printed. It is taken with him as a word for crying out (?), by its classifier; the reading is doubtful. The last word has only s, b and t, with the stick (coded M3, approximate) and the man with hand to mouth, the classifiers that sdbḥ 'entreat' (?) has at the fifth pylon: it is taken as that word written short, with d and ḥ not written (Budge: setebḥ), here as a noun after tnwt. The reading is doubtful.

sentences.n: nrw 'terror' is r set over water n, then w, a vulture's head on a coiled neck (coded G14, approximate), U15 and a stroke: the vulture is the classifier of fear, as in the name of the first doorkeeper, Neruyt (Budge: neru). r and n stand in the group in the reverse order. n 'through, because of' is water n. šfšft·s 'her awe' is the pool š (coded N37, approximate) and the viper f written twice, t, a ram's head (coded F7, approximate), the narrow sign Y1a, a stroke and the folded cloth ·s: šfšft, the dread a god inspires, which takes the ram as its classifier.

sentences.l: not · fears · for-her · the-one-who · is-in · inside-her
sentences.i: The one who is within her has no fear of her.
sentences.n: n 'not' is the arms held out (coded D35, approximate) with water n as complement. Budge's group senṭ - nes is split here into two words: snḏ 'fear', the trussed goose (coded G54, approximate) standing for the word, with the man with hand to mouth, a sḏm·f after n; and n·s, water n with the bolt ·s, 'for her, because of her'. nty 'who' is water n, t and two strokes y: the relative adjective used as a noun, 'the one who', here the subject of snḏ. m 'in' is the owl. ẖnw·s 'her inside' begins with a slim animal sign (coded E14, approximate) that stands for ẖn, as in ẖnw in the address of Spell 125, with water n as complement, then the pot nw, w and the house, with ·s: m ẖnw 'within'. The pylon is a terror to those outside, but whoever is inside her need not fear. Budge reads the n·s as the n of the sḏm·n·f, 'she does not fear (whoever is within)'; that is possible, and the sense is doubtful.

sentences.i: The name of its doorkeeper: Sekhen-wer.
sentences.n: rn n iry-ꜥꜣ·s, with iry spelled out (a reed, r, two strokes y and the herdsman), the hatched sign O29 (approximate) for ꜥꜣ over U15 (not read), and the bolt ·s; Budge prints àri āa - s as one group here. The name is the folded cloth s, ḫ and n with two embracing arms (coded D32, approximate) as classifier, then the swallow wr with r, and the squatting man with a flail (A52) as the classifier of a person: sḫn-wr, 'Great Embracer', from sḫn 'embrace' and wr 'great' (Budge: Seχen-ur). The tenth pylon ends here, and with it Spell 146 on Ani's papyrus. Other papyri go on with further pylons (Budge's Appendix gives pylons 11 to 21 from Naville's Todtenbuch), which Ani's papyrus does not have.

glossary.dyw: dyw — fifty (numeral; the script almost never spells it out, writing the figure instead)
glossary.m: m — in, from (preposition) · also "with" (instrument), "as" (m bnw "as the Bennu"), "on" (living on), "by"; im before a suffix (im·i, im·f, im·tn) · a second word of the same spelling: what? (interrogative pronoun; r m 'for what? why?') · also 'among' (with a group of people) · also the negative imperative 'do not!' (before a verb form: m irt 'do not make'; from the verb imi) · also written mꜥ, with the arm · also "of, made of" (naming the material a thing is made of)
glossary.dbn: dbn — to go round, encircle (verb); circuit (noun; Budge: ṭeben)
glossary.sꜣtt: sꜣtt — covered, overlaid (?) (not identified; the sense is guessed from the context and is doubtful; Budge: satet)
glossary.wꜣḏ: wꜣḏ — papyrus stem; papyrus-column, papyrus-sceptre or amulet (noun) · also green, fresh, flourishing (adjective; verb wꜣḏ 'be green') (Budge: 'tablet') · also fresh plants, greens, vegetables (noun) · also green stone (noun; written with the stone as classifier; Budge: uat')
glossary.šmꜥ: šmꜥ — the South, Upper Egypt (noun m.; Budge: qemāu, his old value for the sign)
glossary.ṯs: ṯs — to tie, knot; to raise up; to marshal, command (verb)
glossary.qq: qq — to eat (?) (verb; written with the man with hand to mouth, the classifier of eating and speaking; doubtful; Budge: qeq)
glossary.ir-sw-ḏs-f: ir-sw-ḏs-f — Ir-su-djes-ef, 'He who made himself by himself', the doorkeeper of the ninth pylon of Spell 146 (name of a gatekeeper demon; from iri 'make', sw 'him' and ḏs·f 'himself'; Budge: Àri-su t'esef)
glossary.mḥ: mḥ — to fill, fill up (verb; mḥ wḏꜣt 'fill the Eye', make it whole) · also forms the ordinals from ten upward, mḥ with the number, 'the one that completes N' (participle; mḥt-mḏ 'tenth', feminine; Budge: meḥt met)
glossary.mḏ: mḏ — ten (numeral; the word behind the sign for ten; in ordinals mḥt-mḏ 'tenth'; Budge: met)
glossary.qꜣ: qꜣ — high, exalted (adjective; verb qꜣi 'be high'); as a noun, 'the High One'
glossary.nhs: nhs — to wake, rouse (verb; Budge: neheset)
glossary.tnwt: tnwt — a cry, outcry (?) (noun; the sense comes from the classifier of speech; reading doubtful; Budge: tenàut)
glossary.sdbḥ: sdbḥ — to entreat (?) (verb; causative of dbḥ 'ask for, require'; perhaps instead 'provide for, equip'; doubtful; Budge: seṭebḥ) · also entreaty, supplication (?) (noun; the verb used as a noun; doubtful)
glossary.šfšft: šfšft — dread, awe, the fear a god inspires (noun f.; written with a small ram; Budge: śefśefet, śefśeft)
glossary.nty: nty — who, which, that (relative adjective); as a noun "he who"
glossary.ẖnw: ẖnw — the inside, interior, residence (noun; m ẖnw 'within')
glossary.sḫn-wr: sḫn-wr — Sekhen-wer, 'Great Embracer', the doorkeeper of the tenth pylon of Spell 146 (name of a gatekeeper demon; from sḫn 'embrace' and wr 'great'; Budge: Seχen-ur)
